newsitem.title: JAPAN: Korea Container says may boost samurai issues.
newsitem.headline: Korea Container says may boost samurai issues.

text.p: South Korea's state-owned Korea Container Terminal Co may increase its samurai bond issues to about 10 billion yen or more a year starting in 1997, a senior company official said on Friday.
Korean Container is scheduled to launch its first samurai bond next week. The amount is expected to be five billion yen with a duration of five years.

"This is the first time we have raised funds overseas. Depending on the results of an upcoming samurai launch, we may increase the volume up to about 10 billion yen or more every year starting next year," said Choon-Kil Lee, vice-president of the company's planning section.

Lee spoke at a seminar of about 100 Japanese at the main office of Kokusai Securities, which will act as a lead manager for the issue. It will be the first time Kokusai has acted as a lead manager of this sort.
The maturity date of the bonds will be October 18, 2001, and the payment date will be October 18, 1996.
The subscription period will be between October 16 and October 17. Sakura Bank will act as a lead trustee.
Korea Container was given a preliminary rating of double A plus (AA+) for the issue from Japan Bond Research Institute on August 14.
